subject: Literature
title: The Lost Generation and Hemingway's Iceberg
description: A quick win: understand The Lost Generation and Hemingway's Iceberg.

hook.text: After World War One shattered Europe, a group of disillusioned American writers gathered in Paris cafés.

buildup.text: Hemingway, Fitzgerald, and Gertrude Stein formed the Lost Generation, writing about a world drained of meaning.

discovery.text: Hemingway developed the iceberg theory: show only the surface and let readers feel the hidden emotion beneath.

twist.text: His spare, stripped-down prose was the opposite of the ornate Victorian style, and critics called it primitive.

climax.text: The iceberg theory became one of the most imitated techniques in modern fiction and journalism worldwide.

punchline.text: Hemingway proved that what you leave out matters most.

quiz.question: What is Hemingway's iceberg theory?
options: Novels should be set in cold climates
Show only the surface and let readers feel the hidden emotion beneath
Every sentence should contain at least one metaphor
